purpose: machine-readable ontology for the formal/mathematical layer of feedback loops: analysis and design work-units that quantify, tune, and stabilize feedback systems (feedback control, system response, stability analysis, nonlinear dynamics), as a subdomain node of systems thinking, feedback loops & control for a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: Control Theory & Stability is modeled as the formal/mathematical subdomain of systems thinking, feedback loops & control.
Nodes are concrete, evaluable analysis/design work-units that quantify, tune, and stabilize feedback systems, not generic systems-thinking topics.
No observed dataset or experimental evidence is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Scope follows classical/modern control and nonlinear-dynamics practice (Franklin, Powell & Emami-Naeini 2019; Ogata 2010; Strogatz 2015).
exclusions: Qualitative systems thinking, causal-loop diagramming, and stock-and-flow modeling without the mathematical control layer.
Control hardware, embedded implementation, and real-time software engineering.
Estimation/Kalman filtering and optimal/MPC theory except as they bear on loop stability and tuning.
Plant first-principles physics and sensor/actuator instrumentation design.

competency_questions.question: Given a regulated process, what is the well-posed control objective and quantified performance/stability spec?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTROL_PROBLEM_FRAME maps the goal to a measurable spec

competency_questions.question: What dynamic model (transfer function / state-space) represents the plant and over what validity range?
Should control be open-loop or closed-loop, with what error signal and feedforward, and where is feedback closed?
What controller structure (PID terms) and gain set meet the spec?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PID_CONTROLLER and GAIN_TUNING present and ordered

competency_questions.question: How are gains traded between response speed and stability margin?
What are the transient, steady-state-error, overshoot/damping, and rise/settling-time characteristics?
How do dominant poles/eigenvalues and margins determine closed-loop stability and overshoot?
Where are the system's equilibria/fixed points and is each one stable (Lyapunov)?
How does feedback delay erode margins and what is the tolerable delay before instability?
What gain and phase margins certify robustness of the design?
Does the loop exhibit self-sustained oscillation, limit cycles, or hysteresis-driven behavior, and why?
At what parameter values does behavior change qualitatively (bifurcation) or become chaotic/sensitive to initial conditions?
Is the design robust to model uncertainty, disturbance, delay, and nonlinearity before deployment?
What does a complete, reusable control-design handoff contain for safe implementation and retuning?

glossary.definition: the reference value the controlled variable is driven toward
reference minus measured output, the input to the feedback controller
a control structure that feeds the measured output back to compute the control action
a proportional-integral-derivative control law on the error signal
a dimensionless measure (zeta) of how oscillatory a second-order response is
the residual offset between reference and output as time goes to infinity
a state where the dynamics produce no change (a fixed point of the system)
stability of an equilibrium certified by a decreasing energy-like function
the additional phase lag at gain crossover that would make the loop marginally unstable
an isolated self-sustained periodic orbit of a nonlinear system
a qualitative change in system behavior as a parameter crosses a critical value
bounded deterministic dynamics with sensitive dependence on initial conditions

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established control-theory and nonlinear-dynamics literature (Franklin, Powell & Emami-Naeini, Feedback Control of Dynamic Systems; Ogata, Modern Control Engineering; Strogatz, Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos) and standard engineering practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: State the control objective as a well-posed loop: regulated variable, reference/setpoint, actuator, disturbance, and performance/stability spec, before any controller is designed.
contradictors: analyst who tunes a loop before defining its objective

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when control objective, regulated variable, or performance spec changes

pros.claim: an explicit objective prevents spec-controller mismatch downstream
pros.example: specify 2% settling-time and <5% overshoot targets before picking PID gains

cons.claim: an ill-posed objective makes every later stability and tuning step undefined
cons.example: 'make it stable' with no spec yields no acceptance criterion

acceptance_tests: objective stated as measurable spec on a named regulated variable
actuator, sensor, and disturbance classes enumerated

nodes.definition: Represent the process to be controlled as a dynamic model (transfer function, state-space, or identified empirical model) that the loop analysis and design will use.
contradictors: practitioner who designs a controller with no plant model

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when plant dynamics, operating point, or model uncertainty change

pros.claim: a validated model lets stability and response be predicted before hardware
pros.example: fit a first-order-plus-deadtime model to step-test data

cons.claim: an inaccurate or wrong-order model makes every downstream margin estimate untrustworthy
cons.example: ignoring an unmodeled resonance yields optimistic phase margin

acceptance_tests: model reproduces observed step/frequency response within tolerance
validity range and uncertainty stated

nodes.definition: Decide and structure feedforward/open-loop versus feedback/closed-loop control, fixing the loop topology, measured signals, and where feedback is closed.
contradictors: designer who closes a loop without measuring the regulated variable

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when loop topology or measured-signal availability changes

pros.claim: closing the loop adds disturbance rejection and reduces sensitivity to model error
pros.example: feedback corrects load disturbances an open-loop schedule cannot

cons.claim: feedback introduces the possibility of instability that open-loop control avoids
cons.example: high-gain feedback on a delayed plant can oscillate

failure_modes: feedback closed on an unobservable variable
acceptance_tests: loop topology justified against objective
every feedback signal is measurable

nodes.definition: Define the reference/setpoint and the error signal (reference minus measured output) that drives the controller.
contradictors: engineer who feeds raw output, not error, to the controller

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when setpoint definition, units, or feedback sign change

pros.claim: a correctly signed error makes the loop corrective rather than divergent
pros.example: negative feedback: e=r-y drives y toward r

cons.claim: a sign or units error turns negative feedback into positive feedback and instability
cons.example: swapped sign makes the loop run away

acceptance_tests: error defined as reference minus measured output with consistent units
feedback sign verified negative

nodes.definition: Specify a PID (proportional-integral-derivative) control law mapping the error signal to the actuator command, including which terms are active.
contradictors: engineer who adds derivative action on a noisy measurement without filtering

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when control-law structure or active PID terms change

pros.claim: PID handles a large fraction of practical loops with three interpretable terms
pros.example: integral action removes steady-state offset under constant load

cons.claim: derivative action amplifies measurement noise and integral action causes windup if unmanaged
cons.example: pure D on noisy sensor injects high-frequency actuator chatter

acceptance_tests: control law mapping error to command is fully specified
anti-windup defined when actuator can saturate

nodes.definition: Select controller gains (Kp, Ki, Kd or state-feedback gains) to meet the performance and stability spec, via tuning rules, loop-shaping, or pole placement.
contradictors: practitioner who raises gain until it oscillates and backs off blindly

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when gains, tuning rule, or performance-margin trade change

pros.claim: systematic tuning trades response speed against stability margin explicitly
pros.example: IMC tuning sets gains from a chosen closed-loop time constant

cons.claim: aggressive gains shrink stability margins and amplify noise and disturbances
cons.example: high Kp gives fast response but low phase margin and ringing

acceptance_tests: gains meet performance spec while preserving required stability margins
tuning verified on plant model and uncertainty

nodes.definition: Add feedforward action from a measured reference or measurable disturbance to improve tracking/rejection without relying solely on feedback error.
contradictors: engineer who relies on feedforward alone with no feedback correction

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when feedforward source or model-inverse design changes

pros.claim: feedforward acts before error appears, improving tracking and measurable-disturbance rejection
pros.example: feedforward a known load change to cut transient deviation

cons.claim: feedforward depends on model accuracy and cannot correct unmeasured disturbances
cons.example: an inverted-model feedforward errs when the plant model is wrong

acceptance_tests: feedforward improves tracking/rejection without degrading closed-loop stability

nodes.definition: Characterize the loop's transient (transient vs steady-state) response to reference/disturbance changes as the basis for performance specs.
contradictors: analyst who reports only final value and ignores transient behavior

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when closed-loop dynamics or test scenario change

pros.claim: transient analysis exposes ringing, sluggishness, and instability before deployment
pros.example: a step response reveals an underdamped overshoot the spec forbids

cons.claim: a linear transient analysis can miss nonlinear or saturation-driven behavior
cons.example: actuator saturation makes the real transient differ from the linear prediction

failure_modes: ignoring transient in favor of steady-state
acceptance_tests: transient and steady-state components separated and quantified

nodes.definition: Quantify residual steady-state error to reference/disturbance inputs and relate it to system type and integral action.
contradictors: engineer who expects zero offset from a proportional-only loop

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when input class or system type changes

pros.claim: error constants predict residual offset from system type before testing
pros.example: a type-1 system has zero step error but finite ramp error

cons.claim: adding integrators to kill error can erode stability margin and slow the loop
cons.example: integral action removes offset but adds phase lag near crossover

acceptance_tests: steady-state error computed for the relevant input class and matched to spec

nodes.definition: Relate overshoot and oscillation to the damping ratio and dominant poles so the response meets overshoot/ringing limits.
contradictors: analyst who treats every loop as first-order and ignores overshoot

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when dominant-pole structure or overshoot spec changes

pros.claim: damping ratio gives a direct overshoot prediction for dominant second-order loops
pros.example: zeta=0.7 yields ~5% overshoot in a standard second-order loop

cons.claim: the second-order approximation fails when extra poles/zeros or nonlinearity dominate
cons.example: a nearby zero adds overshoot the damping ratio alone underpredicts

acceptance_tests: overshoot predicted from damping ratio and matched to spec
dominant-pole assumption checked

nodes.definition: Quantify speed-of-response metrics (rise time, settling time) and trade them against overshoot and actuator effort.
contradictors: engineer who maximizes speed with no settling-band or effort limit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when speed metrics or settling-band definition change

pros.claim: settling and rise time make the speed spec testable and comparable across designs
pros.example: 2% settling time gives an unambiguous acceptance threshold

cons.claim: pushing speed shrinks damping and raises actuator effort and noise sensitivity
cons.example: halving rise time can double overshoot and saturate the actuator

acceptance_tests: rise/settling time computed against the named settling band and speed spec

nodes.definition: Locate equilibria/fixed points of the (possibly nonlinear) system and classify them as the foundation for stability analysis.
contradictors: analyst who studies stability without locating the equilibrium

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when equilibrium set or operating point changes

pros.claim: fixed points define where stability is even meaningful to assess
pros.example: a pendulum has stable-down and unstable-up equilibria

cons.claim: nonlinear systems can have multiple or moving equilibria that a single linearization misses
cons.example: a bistable system has two stable states a local model hides

failure_modes: evaluating stability away from a fixed point
acceptance_tests: all relevant equilibria located and classified
operating point identified as a fixed point

nodes.definition: Establish stability of an equilibrium via Lyapunov's direct/indirect methods, certifying stability or asymptotic stability without solving the dynamics.
contradictors: engineer who declares stability from a single simulation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when equilibrium, model, or claimed stability region changes

pros.claim: a Lyapunov certificate proves stability over a region without solving the trajectory
pros.example: V=energy decreasing proves a damped oscillator settles

cons.claim: finding a Lyapunov function is hard and a failed search does not prove instability
cons.example: no found V leaves stability undecided rather than disproved

acceptance_tests: a valid Lyapunov certificate or linearization argument supports the stability claim
region of attraction stated

nodes.definition: Determine closed-loop stability and dominant dynamics from pole/eigenvalue locations of the linearized loop and the role of feedback.
contradictors: analyst who judges stability from output shape alone

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when closed-loop poles, gain, or linearization point change

pros.claim: LHP poles give a clean necessary-and-sufficient linear stability test
pros.example: all closed-loop poles in the left half-plane implies asymptotic stability

cons.claim: pole-based stability is local to the linearization and silent on nonlinear behavior
cons.example: a linearly stable equilibrium can still have a small region of attraction

failure_modes: judging nonlinear stability from linear poles
acceptance_tests: all closed-loop poles/eigenvalues lie in the stable region for the design gains
marginal cases flagged

nodes.definition: Analyze how feedback/transport delay erodes phase and can destabilize an otherwise-stable loop, and bound tolerable delay.
contradictors: engineer who tunes high gain ignoring loop deadtime

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when loop delay, sampling, or gain change

pros.claim: quantifying delay margin prevents high-gain loops from oscillating in deployment
pros.example: deadtime adds phase lag that consumes the phase margin

cons.claim: delay interacts nonlinearly with gain and is easy to underestimate from a no-delay model
cons.example: a model that omits sensor lag overestimates the safe gain

acceptance_tests: delay margin computed and tolerable delay bounded against measured loop delay

nodes.definition: Quantify robustness of closed-loop stability via gain and phase margins from the open-loop frequency response.
contradictors: engineer who reports only nominal stability with no margin

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when open-loop frequency response or robustness target changes

pros.claim: margins certify how much gain/phase error the loop tolerates before instability
pros.example: 6 dB gain margin and 45 deg phase margin is a common robustness target

cons.claim: margins from a nominal model can be optimistic under unmodeled dynamics or delay
cons.example: an unmodeled resonance can collapse an apparently safe phase margin

acceptance_tests: gain and phase margins meet the robustness target for the design
computed from validated model

nodes.definition: Detect and analyze self-sustained oscillations and limit cycles arising from nonlinearity, saturation, or relay/hysteretic feedback.
contradictors: engineer who blames a sensor for an actuator-saturation limit cycle

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when nonlinearity, saturation, or oscillation behavior changes

pros.claim: describing functions predict limit-cycle amplitude and frequency from the nonlinearity
pros.example: relay feedback produces a predictable self-oscillation used for autotuning

cons.claim: limit cycles are invisible to a linear model and depend sensitively on the nonlinearity
cons.example: actuator saturation creates a cycle no linear pole analysis shows

failure_modes: misattributing a nonlinear cycle to linear instability
acceptance_tests: self-sustained oscillation detected and its nonlinear cause identified
amplitude/frequency estimated

nodes.definition: Model hysteresis (history/path-dependent, multivalued response) in the plant or controller and its effect on switching, dead-bands, and oscillation.
contradictors: analyst who models a hysteretic actuator as single-valued

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when hysteresis characteristics or dead-band settings change

pros.claim: intentional hysteresis prevents chatter around a switching threshold
pros.example: a thermostat dead-band stops rapid on/off cycling

cons.claim: unmodeled hysteresis causes limit cycles, offset, and non-repeatable response
cons.example: backlash hysteresis in a gear train degrades positioning accuracy

failure_modes: modeling a hysteretic element as memoryless
dead-band too narrow (chatter) or too wide (offset)
acceptance_tests: hysteresis/dead-band represented and its switching/oscillation effect bounded

nodes.definition: Analyze how qualitative system behavior (number/stability of equilibria, onset of oscillation) changes as a parameter crosses a bifurcation.
contradictors: analyst who assumes stability is parameter-independent

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when parameter ranges or qualitative-behavior regimes change

pros.claim: bifurcation analysis finds the parameter thresholds where the loop changes character
pros.example: a Hopf bifurcation marks the gain at which sustained oscillation begins

cons.claim: bifurcations are global and need nonlinear analysis a local model cannot provide
cons.example: a fold bifurcation triggers sudden collapse a linear model never warns of

acceptance_tests: parameter ranges that change qualitative behavior identified and bounded away from operating point
revisit_triggers: operating parameter shifts toward a critical value

nodes.definition: Identify deterministic chaos and sensitivity to initial conditions, bounding predictability horizons and ruling chaos in or out for the loop.
contradictors: analyst who treats irregular output as random noise

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when parameter regime or chaos evidence changes

pros.claim: a positive Lyapunov exponent certifies chaos and bounds how far prediction is meaningful
pros.example: a chaotic loop's state is unpredictable beyond a finite horizon

cons.claim: distinguishing chaos from noise or transients needs care and long clean data
cons.example: short or noisy records mimic chaos and cause false positives

failure_modes: ignoring chaos in a sensitive regime
over-long prediction of a chaotic state
acceptance_tests: chaos ruled in or out with a Lyapunov-exponent estimate
predictability horizon stated when chaotic

nodes.definition: Validate the closed-loop design against model uncertainty, disturbances, delay, and nonlinearity before any deployment or lock.
contradictors: engineer who locks a design from a single nominal simulation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when uncertainty set, disturbance scenarios, or spec change

pros.claim: robustness validation catches optimistic nominal designs before costly deployment
pros.example: Monte-Carlo over model parameters exposes a margin that nominal analysis hid

cons.claim: validation is only as good as the uncertainty set and tested scenarios
cons.example: an untested disturbance class can still destabilize a 'validated' loop

acceptance_tests: design meets spec and margins across the declared uncertainty and disturbance set
nonlinear and delay scenarios tested

nodes.definition: Package the validated controller, model assumptions, margins, and operating limits into a reusable handoff artifact for implementation or downstream sessions.
contradictors: engineer who ships gains with no model, margins, or operating limits

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when validated design, operating envelope, or assumptions change

pros.claim: a complete handoff lets implementation and later sessions reuse the design safely
pros.example: the artifact states gains, margins, validity range, and retune triggers together

cons.claim: an incomplete handoff forces rework or unsafe operation outside the validated envelope
cons.example: shipping gains without the validity range invites use on the wrong plant

acceptance_tests: handoff artifact contains controller, model, margins, operating limits, and retune triggers

edges.why_related: the objective and spec define what the plant model must capture
edges.risk_of_conflict: modeling before framing yields an over/under-detailed model
edges.example: spec sets needed model fidelity

edges.why_related: the objective determines whether feedback is needed
edges.risk_of_conflict: choosing topology before the goal misfits the loop
edges.example: disturbance-rejection need drives closing the loop

edges.why_related: the model shows controllability and observability that constrain topology
edges.risk_of_conflict: topology chosen without dynamics can be infeasible
edges.example: model reveals an uncontrollable mode

edges.why_related: a closed loop requires a defined error signal
edges.risk_of_conflict: no error signal means no feedback law
edges.example: closing the loop needs r-y

edges.why_related: the PID law operates on the error signal
edges.risk_of_conflict: a controller with no error definition is undefined
edges.example: PID needs e(t)

edges.why_related: controller structure choices depend on plant dynamics
edges.risk_of_conflict: structure picked without the model can misfit
edges.example: integral term chosen for a type-0 plant

edges.why_related: gains are selected for a chosen controller structure
edges.risk_of_conflict: tuning with no structure is ill-defined
edges.example: tune Kp,Ki,Kd of the chosen PID

edges.why_related: feedforward is added relative to the chosen loop topology
edges.risk_of_conflict: feedforward without a topology is unplaced
edges.example: 2-DOF structure fixes feedforward path

edges.why_related: transient response is derived from the model dynamics
edges.risk_of_conflict: response claimed without a model is unsupported
edges.example: step response computed from the model

edges.why_related: steady-state is the limit of the transient and is analyzed after it
edges.risk_of_conflict: mixing transient and steady-state confuses both
edges.example: final-value taken after transient analysis

edges.why_related: integral action changes the steady-state error
edges.risk_of_conflict: adding integrators blindly costs stability
edges.example: integral term zeros step offset
edges.resolution_rule: add integrators only as error requires

edges.why_related: overshoot and damping follow from dominant-pole locations
edges.risk_of_conflict: damping claimed without poles is ungrounded
edges.example: zeta read from dominant complex poles

edges.why_related: overshoot/damping refine the transient characterization
edges.risk_of_conflict: out-of-order analysis duplicates work
edges.example: characterize response then quantify damping

edges.why_related: settling/rise time depend on damping and dominant dynamics
edges.risk_of_conflict: speed metrics without damping mislead
edges.example: settling time scales with damping and frequency

edges.why_related: equilibria are computed from the system model
edges.risk_of_conflict: stability without equilibria is undefined
edges.example: solve f(x*)=0 from the model

edges.why_related: Lyapunov stability is assessed about a located equilibrium
edges.benefit_of_coupling: stability tied to a fixed point
edges.risk_of_conflict: Lyapunov analysis with no equilibrium is meaningless
edges.example: prove V decreasing about x*

edges.why_related: eigenvalues are evaluated at the linearization about an equilibrium
edges.risk_of_conflict: poles computed away from a fixed point misclassify stability
edges.example: Jacobian eigenvalues at x*

edges.why_related: closed-loop poles come from the model and feedback
edges.risk_of_conflict: poles without a model are guesses
edges.example: characteristic polynomial from the model

edges.why_related: margins quantify robustness of the pole-based stability
edges.risk_of_conflict: nominal stability without margins is fragile
edges.example: margins from the open-loop response

edges.why_related: delay shifts the effective poles toward instability
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring delay overestimates stability
edges.example: deadtime erodes the stable pole configuration

edges.why_related: delay margin is read against the phase margin
edges.risk_of_conflict: delay analysis without phase margin is incomplete
edges.example: phase margin divided by crossover gives delay margin

edges.why_related: margin shortfall triggers retuning of the gains
edges.risk_of_conflict: tuning that ignores margins can destabilize
edges.example: low phase margin sends gains back for retuning
edges.resolution_rule: retune until margins meet target; stop when both within target

edges.why_related: poor transient performance triggers retuning
edges.risk_of_conflict: tuning without checking response wastes effort
edges.example: overshoot over spec sends gains back
edges.resolution_rule: retune until response meets spec; stop at conformance

edges.why_related: limit cycles are analyzed relative to (unstable) equilibria
edges.risk_of_conflict: cycle analysis with no fixed point is unfocused
edges.example: a limit cycle encircles an unstable focus

edges.why_related: controller gain and saturation can induce limit cycles
edges.risk_of_conflict: high gain into saturation oscillates
edges.example: integral windup plus saturation sustains a cycle
edges.resolution_rule: reduce gain or add anti-windup; stop when cycle removed

edges.why_related: both concern multivalued/history-dependent state structure
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating memoryless equilibria with hysteresis misleads
edges.example: bistability vs hysteretic memory

edges.why_related: bifurcation tracks how equilibria appear/disappear/change stability
edges.risk_of_conflict: bifurcation analysis with no equilibrium baseline is undefined
edges.example: a saddle-node creates/destroys fixed points

edges.why_related: stability change at a parameter is a bifurcation
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring stability change misses the bifurcation
edges.example: a Hopf occurs as an equilibrium loses stability

edges.why_related: routes to chaos pass through bifurcation cascades
edges.risk_of_conflict: chaos analysis with no bifurcation context is unanchored
edges.example: a period-doubling cascade precedes chaos

edges.why_related: chaos is assessed after fixed-point and bifurcation structure is known
edges.risk_of_conflict: jumping to chaos skips needed structure
edges.example: map the dynamics before testing for chaos

edges.why_related: the tuned design is the object that validation stresses
edges.risk_of_conflict: validating before tuning is premature
edges.example: stress the final gains against uncertainty

edges.why_related: margins are inputs to the robustness verdict
edges.risk_of_conflict: validation without margins is incomplete
edges.example: check margins hold across the uncertainty set

edges.why_related: delay tolerance is a robustness condition to validate
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring delay in validation is unsafe
edges.example: verify the loop survives worst-case delay

edges.why_related: the stability certificate is validated over the operating region
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unvalidated certificate may not hold globally
edges.example: confirm the region of attraction covers operation

edges.why_related: only a validated design may be packaged for handoff
edges.risk_of_conflict: handing off an unvalidated design causes downstream rework
edges.example: ship gains only after validation passes

edges.why_related: the handoff records the final tuned gains
edges.risk_of_conflict: handoff without final gains is useless
edges.example: artifact lists Kp,Ki,Kd and validity range

edges.why_related: faster response trades against stability margin
edges.risk_of_conflict: chasing speed shrinks margins toward instability
edges.example: high Kp gives speed but low phase margin
edges.resolution_rule: when margin < target, robustness dominates; cap gain

edges.why_related: increasing speed reduces damping and raises overshoot
edges.risk_of_conflict: minimizing settling time can violate the overshoot spec
edges.example: faster rise time increases percent overshoot
edges.resolution_rule: decision-required: pick the spec-binding metric; overshoot limit dominates safety-critical loops

edges.why_related: feedforward performance depends on model accuracy it cannot itself verify
edges.risk_of_conflict: aggressive model-inverse feedforward amplifies model error
edges.example: an inverted-model feedforward errs with model mismatch
edges.resolution_rule: when model uncertainty is high, limit feedforward aggressiveness; feedback dominates

edges.why_related: adding integral action to cut error erodes phase margin
edges.risk_of_conflict: more integrators reduce stability margin
edges.example: integral lag lowers phase margin near crossover
edges.resolution_rule: when margin is binding, accept residual error or add phase lead; margin dominates

conflict_axes.trigger: raising gain to meet a speed spec shrinks gain/phase margins
resolution_order: fix the minimum required stability margin
tune speed only within that margin
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: required stability margin dominates; speed is maximized subject to it
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a loop is required to be both fastest and most robust simultaneously
conflict_axes.example: a high-Kp loop meets settling time but has 20 deg phase margin

conflict_axes.trigger: a design tuned for the nominal model degrades under uncertainty
resolution_order: require performance to hold across it
accept lower nominal performance for robustness
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: robustness across the declared uncertainty set dominates nominal optimality
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: nominal-only performance is locked without an uncertainty check
conflict_axes.example: a sharply tuned loop that only works at one operating point

conflict_axes.trigger: reducing rise time increases overshoot beyond the spec
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the safety/spec-binding metric dominates; overshoot dominates for safety-critical actuation
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: both overshoot and speed are declared hard limits that cannot co-hold
conflict_axes.example: a positioning loop that overshoots a hard mechanical stop to hit a speed target

conflict_axes.trigger: adding integral action to remove offset reduces phase margin
resolution_order: add integral action up to the margin limit
add phase lead if both are binding
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: stability margin dominates; residual error is accepted or compensated with lead
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: zero error and full margin are both demanded on a delayed plant
conflict_axes.example: a third integrator that zeros ramp error but rings

conflict_axes.trigger: feedforward speed depends on a model that may be wrong
resolution_order: rely on feedback for the residual
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: feedback correction dominates under model uncertainty; feedforward is a bounded add-on
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: feedforward is used as the sole controller on an uncertain plant
conflict_axes.example: a model-inverse feedforward that overshoots when the gain is mis-estimated

conflict_axes.trigger: a linear analysis is tractable but can miss nonlinear instability
resolution_order: check nonlinear behavior in the operating envelope
escalate to nonlinear methods when nonlinearity is significant
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: nonlinear evidence dominates a linear verdict whenever nonlinearity is material
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a linearly stable design operates where saturation or bifurcation matters
conflict_axes.example: a linearly stable loop that limit-cycles under actuator saturation

conflict_axes.trigger: a simple controller is preferred but deep analysis is costly
resolution_order: match analysis depth to risk and irreversibility
do full nonlinear analysis for high-risk loops
keep PID where linear analysis suffices
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: risk/irreversibility dominates: high-risk loops require completeness over simplicity
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a high-irreversibility loop is shipped on linear analysis alone
conflict_axes.example: skipping bifurcation analysis on a loop that operates near a Hopf point

conflict_axes.trigger: autotuning produces gains for a safety-relevant, irreversible loop
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: human review dominates automation for high-risk or irreversible loops
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: autotuned gains are hard-locked without review on a safety loop
conflict_axes.example: shipping autotuner output to a flight actuator with no review

conflict_axes.trigger: aggressive commands drive the actuator into saturation or chatter
resolution_order: add anti-windup and dead-band as needed
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: actuator limits and chatter-avoidance dominate raw aggressiveness
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: gains are pushed past actuator capability to hit a speed target
conflict_axes.example: a high-gain loop that windup-cycles around saturation

edge_cases.trigger: stability is claimed from linear poles while the loop saturates
edge_cases.failure_mode: a nonlinear limit cycle is missed
edge_cases.example: a linearly stable loop oscillates in deployment due to actuator saturation
edge_cases.detection_method: compare linear stability claim against a nonlinear/saturated simulation

edge_cases.trigger: the model omits loop deadtime and gains are set on a no-delay model
edge_cases.failure_mode: a real loop oscillates from delay-induced phase loss
edge_cases.example: tuning that looks robust on the no-delay model goes unstable with sensor lag
edge_cases.detection_method: check whether measured loop delay is represented in the model used for margins
resolution: add the transport delay to the model

edge_cases.trigger: the error sign is wrong, turning negative feedback into positive feedback
edge_cases.example: a swapped feedback sign makes the output run away from the setpoint
edge_cases.detection_method: verify feedback polarity makes e=r-y corrective on a small step
resolution: re-verify polarity on a bench step test

edge_cases.trigger: integral action accumulates while the actuator is saturated
edge_cases.failure_mode: large overshoot or a sustained limit cycle
edge_cases.example: a saturating valve with integral action overshoots badly on recovery
edge_cases.detection_method: check for anti-windup whenever the actuator can saturate

edge_cases.trigger: overshoot is predicted from a dominant second-order approximation that fails
edge_cases.example: a nearby zero adds overshoot the damping-ratio estimate underpredicts
edge_cases.detection_method: compare second-order prediction against the full-model step response
resolution: use the full model for overshoot

edge_cases.trigger: a second equilibrium or nearby bifurcation is missed
edge_cases.failure_mode: unexpected state switch or collapse in operation
edge_cases.example: a bistable loop jumps to an unanalyzed state under disturbance
edge_cases.detection_method: scan the parameter/operating range for additional equilibria and bifurcations
resolution: bound the operating point away from bifurcations

edge_cases.trigger: irregular deterministic output is mislabeled as random noise
edge_cases.example: a chaotic regime is filtered as noise instead of being avoided
edge_cases.detection_method: estimate the largest Lyapunov exponent on clean data before labeling noise
resolution: shift operating regime away from chaos

edge_cases.trigger: margins are computed from an inaccurate nominal model
edge_cases.failure_mode: real margins are smaller than reported
edge_cases.example: an unmodeled resonance collapses an apparently safe phase margin
edge_cases.detection_method: recompute margins across the model uncertainty set, not just nominal
resolution: validate the model before trusting margins

edge_cases.trigger: a design is hard-locked before robustness validation and review pass
edge_cases.example: gains are frozen from a single nominal simulation with no review
edge_cases.detection_method: block hard lock until validation gates and human review are recorded
resolution: run validation and review before re-lock

edge_cases.trigger: a performance-robustness tradeoff is encoded as a dependency, not a conflict
edge_cases.failure_mode: the trade is hidden from resolution logic
edge_cases.example: tuning-vs-margin tension modeled as a prerequisite edge loses its resolution rule
edge_cases.detection_method: audit edges where signed_tension is negative but type is not conflict
resolution: re-type the tradeoff as a conflict edge

edge_cases.trigger: actuator hysteresis/backlash is modeled as single-valued
edge_cases.failure_mode: chatter, offset, or a limit cycle appears
edge_cases.example: a hysteretic valve chatters around the switching threshold
edge_cases.detection_method: check whether known hysteresis/backlash is represented in the model
resolution: size the dead-band to stop chatter

edge_cases.trigger: tuning starts before the objective/spec is fixed
edge_cases.failure_mode: gains are tuned to the wrong target
edge_cases.example: a loop is tuned for speed when the real spec was overshoot-limited
edge_cases.detection_method: verify CONTROL_PROBLEM_FRAME is locked before tuning begins

workflow.objective: fix the control objective and performance/stability spec
acceptance_tests: objective stated as a measurable spec
regulated variable named
workflow.do_first_because: the objective is the highest-coupling foundation every later choice inherits

workflow.objective: build and validate a dynamic plant model
acceptance_tests: model reproduces observed response within tolerance
uncertainty stated
workflow.do_first_because: every stability and response result depends on the model

workflow.objective: fix loop topology, error signal, and any feedforward
acceptance_tests: error defined as r-y with correct sign
every feedback signal measurable
workflow.do_first_because: topology and signal definitions gate all controller work

workflow.objective: specify the control law structure and anti-windup
acceptance_tests: control law fully specified
anti-windup defined for saturating actuators
workflow.do_first_because: a defined structure is required before gains or response can be analyzed

workflow.objective: characterize transient, steady-state, overshoot/damping, and speed
acceptance_tests: transient and steady-state separated
overshoot/speed quantified against spec
workflow.do_first_because: response metrics define the tuning targets and feed stability analysis

workflow.objective: establish stability, margins, and delay tolerance
acceptance_tests: all closed-loop poles in the stable region
margins and delay margin meet targets
workflow.do_first_because: stability and margins are the hard safety foundation gating tuning lock

workflow.objective: check nonlinear behavior in the operating envelope
acceptance_tests: limit cycles and bifurcations bounded away from the operating point
chaos ruled in/out
workflow.do_first_because: nonlinear behavior can invalidate a linearly stable design and must be checked before lock

workflow.objective: select gains meeting performance within stability margins
acceptance_tests: gains meet spec while preserving required margins
workflow.do_first_because: tuning must follow response and stability so it optimizes within validated constraints

workflow.objective: validate the design against uncertainty, disturbance, delay, and nonlinearity
acceptance_tests: spec and margins hold across the uncertainty and disturbance set
nonlinear and delay scenarios pass
workflow.do_first_because: no design may be locked or handed off before robustness validation and review pass

workflow.objective: package the validated design and operating limits for handoff
acceptance_tests: handoff contains controller, model, margins, operating limits, and retune triggers
workflow.do_first_because: a complete validated handoff enables safe reuse and is the only artifact eligible for hard lock

priority_rationale.notes: error signal is the controller input
fixed points anchor stability and nonlinear analysis
linear stability gates margins and damping
gate before any lock or handoff
final reusable artifact, only hard-lock candidate

dominance_rules.trigger: a stakeholder demands faster response than the stability margin allows
dominance_rules.rule: required stability margin must hold before any speed gain is accepted
dominance_rules.required_action: cap gain at the margin limit
dominance_rules.example: refuse gains that drop phase margin below target

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value step is requested before its prerequisite is done
dominance_rules.required_action: block the dependent step until prerequisites pass
dominance_rules.example: do not tune before the spec and model are fixed

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise number is presented with no grounding
dominance_rules.rule: evidence labels dominate apparent numeric precision
dominance_rules.example: a margin estimate stays heuristic without measured data

dominance_rules.trigger: a design is proposed for lock before validation passes
dominance_rules.required_action: block lock until robustness validation passes
dominance_rules.example: no hard lock from a nominal simulation

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or safety-critical loop is designed automatically
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for high-risk/irreversible loops
dominance_rules.required_action: require human sign-off above the risk threshold
dominance_rules.example: review autotuned gains for a flight actuator

dominance_rules.trigger: a design optimizes nominal performance and ignores uncertainty
dominance_rules.rule: robustness across the uncertainty set dominates nominal optimality
dominance_rules.required_action: require performance to hold across the declared uncertainty
dominance_rules.example: reject a loop that only works at one operating point

dominance_rules.trigger: linear and nonlinear analyses disagree where nonlinearity is material
dominance_rules.rule: nonlinear evidence dominates a linear stability verdict when nonlinearity matters
dominance_rules.example: trust the limit-cycle finding over linear stability under saturation

dominance_rules.rule: schema and reference integrity dominate object count
dominance_rules.example: do not add an edge that breaks acyclicity

dominance_rules.trigger: readability is traded against strict JSON validity
dominance_rules.rule: strict JSON validity dominates prose quality
dominance_rules.example: drop commentary to keep the artifact parseable

dominance_rules.trigger: a claim exceeds what the source registry supports
dominance_rules.example: no observed label without observed data

dominance_rules.trigger: a locally optimal step risks downstream rework
dominance_rules.example: fix the estimand-equivalent spec before tuning

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient ordering would introduce a dependency cycle
dominance_rules.required_action: convert the weaker edge to sequence/feedback
dominance_rules.example: make the tuning-margin loop a feedback edge, not a dependency

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the objective and spec before designing any controller
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a controller designed for the wrong spec answers the wrong problem
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: tuning started before the spec is fixed
anti_rework_rules.example: tuning for speed when the spec was overshoot-limited

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate the plant model before any stability or response analysis
anti_rework_rules.rationale: analysis on a wrong model produces untrustworthy margins
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: poles computed before the model is validated
anti_rework_rules.example: reporting phase margin from an unvalidated model

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix loop topology and the error signal before the control law
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a control law with no defined input/topology is undefined
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: controller specified before error is defined
anti_rework_rules.example: writing a PID law with no agreed error signal

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the controller structure before tuning gains
anti_rework_rules.rationale: gains for an unchosen structure are meaningless
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: gains tuned before structure is set
anti_rework_rules.example: tuning Kd before deciding derivative action is used

anti_rework_rules.rationale: stability is undefined without a fixed point to assess

anti_rework_rules.rule: establish stability and margins before locking gains
anti_rework_rules.rationale: gains locked without margins can be unstable in the field
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: gains locked before margins are checked
anti_rework_rules.example: shipping gains with unknown phase margin

anti_rework_rules.rule: check nonlinear behavior in the operating envelope before lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a linearly stable design can limit-cycle or bifurcate in operation
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: design locked with no nonlinear check
anti_rework_rules.example: locking a loop that operates near a Hopf point

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate robustness before any handoff or hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an unvalidated handoff forces downstream rework or unsafe operation
anti_rework_rules.example: handing off gains from a single nominal run

anti_rework_rules.rule: require human review before irreversible/safety-critical lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: irreversible decisions are costly to reverse after the fact
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: hard lock with no review record
anti_rework_rules.example: deploying to an actuator with no sign-off

anti_rework_rules.rule: populate formula variables before computing scores
anti_rework_rules.rationale: scores from missing variables are inconsistent
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: computed score present with no input variables
anti_rework_rules.example: a final_importance with no base metrics

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete the traceability matrix before hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: untraceable artifacts cannot be safely change-controlled
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: hard lock with an incomplete trace
anti_rework_rules.example: locking without linking sources to nodes and validation

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or design review reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.trigger: multiple defects are open at once
iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and irreversibility
action: rank by risk_if_wrong and downstream impact
acceptance_tests: highest-risk defect addressed first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only low-risk warnings remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling node
acceptance_tests: all downstream dependents identified
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set stable across a pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is prioritized for repair
acceptance_tests: each defect has an owner

iteration_protocol.trigger: a repair changed a locked or high-coupling component
iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the validator and affected gates
acceptance_tests: no new failures introduced

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence would change a node's importance
iteration_protocol.detection: recompute posterior and compare to prior
acceptance_tests: posterior recomputed for affected nodes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a dependency cycle or mis-typed edge is found
iteration_protocol.detection: run cycle detection and edge-type audit
acceptance_tests: dependency graph is acyclic
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no cycles and no dep/conflict conflation remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream assumption changed under a locked artifact
acceptance_tests: no dependent stays hard-locked on a changed assumption

iteration_protocol.trigger: risk or irreversibility crosses the review threshold
iteration_protocol.detection: check risk_if_wrong and irreversibility against thresholds
acceptance_tests: high-risk items have a recorded decision

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new KB version is prepared for release
iteration_protocol.detection: compare against the prior version's checks
action: diff counts and check results vs prior
acceptance_tests: no mandatory check regressed
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no regressions versus the prior accepted version
